title: Article 60 — Oath or affirmation by the President

content.overview: Article 60 requires every President and every person acting as President or discharging the functions of the President to, before entering upon his office, make and subscribe in the presence of the Chief Justice of India (or, in his absence, the senior-most Judge of the Supreme Court available) an oath or affirmation in the form set out in the article (to preserve, protect and defend the Constitution and the law and devote himself to the service and well-being of the people of India).
content.glance: Oath before CJI (or senior-most available SC Judge): preserve, protect and defend the Constitution and the law; devote to service and well-being of the people.
content.study:
Article 60 oath/affirmation is taken before the Chief Justice of India or, in his absence, the senior-most Judge of the Supreme Court available. The form commits the President to preserve, protect and defend the Constitution and the law and to devote himself to the service and well-being of the people of India.

Examination: before whom; substance of the oath; applies also to persons acting as / discharging functions of President.

sections.heading: Key rule
sections.body: Before entering upon office, the President (and any person acting as or discharging the functions of President) makes and subscribes the prescribed oath/affirmation in the presence of the CJI or, in his absence, the senior-most available SC Judge.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Before whom does the President take the oath?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 60, the President makes and subscribes the oath or affirmation in the presence of the Chief Justice of India or, in his absence, the senior-most Judge of the Supreme Court available, before entering upon his office.

examTips: Oath before CJI; preserve, protect and defend the Constitution.
